notes.title: GW1 team news: a 75% flag is not a sell signal
paragraphs: 61 players are ruled out for the GW1 deadline and 15 are doubtful. Only two of the doubtful are owned by more than 1%, so most of that list isn't your problem.

Mukiele is the one I'd look at. FPL has him 75% to play, 4.3% own him, and he's still the best six-gameweek projection on the entire doubtful list at 17.0, with the 75% already taken out of the number. The flag costs him less than the panic around it does.
Šeško is the other one over 1%. Same 75%, 2.1% owned, 11.3.
Kroupi is the most owned player who can't play at all, and Bournemouth's cover for him is Tavernier on 26.1. I'd move him and stop reading about it.

notes.title: Defender xG comes in two kinds, and the column doesn't say which
notes.cta: Open the stats page and check any of these
paragraphs: Everyone knows a centre-back's goals come from corners. That part isn't interesting. What surprised me is how badly it works as a rule.

Gabriel finished last season on 4.65 non-penalty xG and 4.50 of it was set pieces. Ninety-seven percent. Sessegnon finished on 2.05 with 0.11 from set pieces. Five percent. Same position, same column, almost nothing in common.

Take the 23 defenders with at least 2.0 non-penalty xG. Ten are above 80% set pieces, six are below 50%, and the other seven are scattered across the middle. There's no typical number to fall back on, which is the problem: the column gives you one figure and it can mean either thing.
The best attacking defender in the sample is in the wrong group for the stereotype. O'Reilly has the highest non-penalty xG of any defender, 6.73, and only 22% of it comes from set pieces.
xG gets treated as one currency. You compare two players, the higher number wins, and for most of the league that's fine, because both numbers are made of the same stuff.

For the defenders at the top of that first table the number comes from somewhere else. It depends on how many set pieces the team wins and on who is delivering them. Neither of those moves with the things that normally move a team's attack.

Take a club that sells its main striker. Open-play creation drops and the rating should drop with it. But the number of set pieces barely changes, and the centre-back who scores off them keeps scoring as long as the delivery is still there.

If you're comparing two defenders on xG, look at what the xG is made of before you trust the gap. A 3.0 that's 90% set pieces and a 3.0 that's 30% set pieces are different bets, and the second one is closer to a normal attacking return.

And if a club changes who takes its corners, that's the transfer that should worry you about a set-piece defender, more than the striker leaving. The same view on the stats page lists the corner and free-kick taker order, so you can check who is on them now. I don't have a clean number for how much delivery quality matters, and I'd rather say that than invent one.

The shot data is 2025/26, not the season about to start. Some of the shares sit on thin samples: Van de Ven's 89% comes off 2.45 npxG, which is about two goals' worth of chances, and I wouldn't lean on it the way I'd lean on Gabriel's 4.65.
Set-piece xG isn't immune to squad change either, it just doesn't respond to the same inputs. A manager who stops loading the box would flatten these numbers quickly.
Set piece here means corners and free kicks, not corners alone. The column doesn't split them, so I'm not going to guess at the split either.

And none of it says whether a player is good. Gabriel at 97% is one of the better attacking defenders in the league, and set-piece goals count the same as any other. The problem is that they run on a different engine, so anything that treats the two as one number will be wrong in a direction you can predict.

Both columns are on our free stats page, no sign-in, but they sit in different views. Easiest route: type the name into "Search player", then switch between "Goal threat" for npxG and "Set pieces" for Set-piece xG. If you want to sort the whole list instead, press "Show all players" first, because the table opens on the top 100 and several of the names above sit outside it on npxG. Basis is 2025/26, 400 players in this season's FPL squads.
